title: Define onboarding signal surface and evidence matrix for new open-model entries
creator: Aisha Khatri
description:
Purpose: Clarify the exact signals (the "signal surface") we will require from contributors of open models and define an evidence matrix that maps each signal to a concrete artifact, test, or measurement. This ticket replaces vague 'compatibility notes' language with a deterministic checklist that operators, runtime engineers, and intake reviewers can use to accept or reject catalog entries.

Scope: Defines required and optional signals, the artifacts that count as evidence, automated gate behavior (pass/warn/fail), how UI exposes pass/fail state, and acceptance criteria for the first rollout. Does NOT implement the UI or ingestion automation (separate ENG tasks).

Problem: Current onboarding language is inconsistent across intake forms and reviewers apply different heuristics when deciding to soft-pin or reject models. This causes operational risk (surprises at runtime), longer intake cycles, and customer confusion about which variant is safe to use.

Goals:
- Create an auditable, machine-checkable evidence matrix for at least 10 signals relevant to runtime stability and compatibility.
- Reduce manual reviewer variance by specifying minimal artifacts per signal (e.g., runtime profile JSON, sample inference harness, license file).
- Produce deterministic pass/warn/fail rules used by automated intake gating.
- Provide acceptance criteria so ENG can implement gates and Console can display signal status.
acceptance_criteria: An evidence matrix document exists listing each signal, required artifacts, acceptable formats, and a priority (required/strongly-recommended/optional)
For each required signal there is at least one automated check described (e.g., runtime smoke with <=2s median token latency on reference hardware) and a fallback behaviour defined (fail vs warn)
Definitions for provenance and license checks are explicit: supported license whitelist and provenance hash format must be specified
Console mockups show a signal-level pass/warn/fail badge and an expandable evidence list for reviewers
A migration guidance section explains how pre-existing catalog entries are re-evaluated and what grace periods apply
Security team approves the required evidence types for private deployments (KMS/HSM usage, restricted binary artifacts) documented
A handoff bundle (evidence matrix + example intake payloads + sample runtime profile) is attached to this ticket for ENG implementation

Will require a short text justification plus unit tests demonstrating tokenization parity for common inputs.

notes: Trade-offs discussed: strict gating reduces risk but increases friction for contributors; suggestion to support two admission channels (experimental with warnings, production with required evidence)
We will pilot the matrix with 10 incoming community submissions and measure review time reduction and post-ingest incidents over a 6-week window
